title: Adding/removing items
learningObjectives: Explain adding/removing items and process JavaScript collections correctly.

understand.concept: Arrays provide methods such as push() and pop() to add or remove items at the end, and unshift() and shift() to add or remove items at the beginning. These methods mutate the original array. Other methods such as slice() return a new array without changing the source.
understand.whyItMatters: Knowing which methods mutate state is important when sharing arrays between parts of an application. Avoid accidental changes to data that other code expects to remain unchanged.
understand.analogy: push adds to the end of a queue; pop removes from the end. shift and unshift work at the beginning.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript array and object methods have defined mutation, iteration, and reference semantics.

explain.narrative: push adds Review and pop removes it again, returning the removed value.

examples.explanation: push adds Review and pop removes it again, returning the removed value.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the array or object values described.

practise.guidedTask: Use push, pop, shift, and unshift on a task list. Record which methods mutate the original array.
practise.independentTask: Build a small collection-processing example using arrays and objects. Test empty collections, missing values, and mutation behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates or returns a new value.
Use clear object property names and deliberate copying.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Adding/removing items</title></head><body>
<script>const tasks=['Read','Practise'];tasks.push('Review');const removed=tasks.pop();console.log(tasks,removed);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which array method adds an item to the end and mutates the array?
questions.explanation: push() adds one or more elements to the end of the array.

questions.prompt: What should you check when using an array method?
options: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
Whether the array contains strings only
questions.answer: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
questions.explanation: Mutation behaviour matters when arrays are shared across application code.
